Decided 2026-11-20 (RC-TOPOLOGY-AUTHORITY-2026-11-20, resolved by the build loop under the maintainer's delegated owner-block authority; no contract text changed): the per-monitor logical-to-physical mapping is implemented with a decided authority - QScreen logical geometry (zxdg_output-derived on Wayland) is the selection space, each display's physical bounds are its own logical extent times its own scale (mode-verified against live wl_output facts), and the packed global arrangement is a documented degraded disposition endorsed only when the compositor's own zxdg_output logical rectangles prove a strict grid tiling (complete facts, unrotated/unflipped, mode-consistent, exact integer tiling check). Gapped, overlapping, staggered, rotated, flipped or silent-xdg arrangements fail closed with compositor-layout-unproven. Sources: grim's logical-space composition and its documented grid-assumption caveat, and KDE Spectacle's compositor-composite crop design. The tiling and mode-consistency rules were each proven red by disabling them; live compositor qualification remains separate.

The RC-022 mapping is decided with the same authority: D.physical.left + (x - D.logical.left) * D.scale in IEEE 754 double, with each display's own mode-verified bounds and the packed origins endorsed only for proven grid tilings (RC-TOPOLOGY-AUTHORITY-2026-11-20). Core floor-epsilon mapping is vector-tested and the new layout rules are tested end-to-end against a fake libwayland server driving the real client binding; unprovable arrangements fail closed. Live compositor qualification remains separate.

The recorded mapping-authority blocker is resolved by RC-TOPOLOGY-AUTHORITY-2026-11-20: the persisted last region's display bounds are the decided per-display own-scale extents, the packed arrangement they live in is endorsed only for proven grid tilings, and recapture on an unproven arrangement fails closed with compositor-layout-unproven rather than capturing misaligned pixels. Native validation (last-region-invalid on missing/changed displays) exists and is decided rather than candidate; live desktop qualification on real mixed-scale/rotated hardware is the remaining physical gate.

The remaining build half of RC-TOPOLOGY-AUTHORITY-2026-11-20 is landed: the compositor-native cursor path composes one desktop from per-output frames on proven grids. Every display is captured by its frozen compositor name (each connection re-proves the whole live layout, so an unprovable grid fails closed inside the capture itself), the compose seam (composeCapturedFrames) cross-checks every frame against the frozen session - compositor name, logical position, scale, mode-verified buffer bounds, provenance - before placing it at the packed origin, and any disagreement refuses whole with compositor-source-mismatch. A cross-monitor confirmed rectangle crops both displays' pixels at the exact packed boundary, proven by the integration test; an unnamed display refuses a priori. The placement and the frame cross-check were each proven red by disabling them. Live desktop qualification on real Sway/mixed-scale/rotated hardware remains the physical gate.

Decided and built 2026-11-23 (backlog item 2's first half, decision EC-013-BACKGROUND-COMPOSITION-2026-11-23, resolved by the build loop under delegated owner-block authority; no contract text change - the SPEC's MUSTs stand and the record settles the open semantics the row named): background composition is one committed, fully undoable canvas operation rather than the reference's view-time state, because this edition's canvas architecture already owns immutable sources plus one-history-entry operations - the smallest reversible model that makes the saved PNG carry the composed background. The decided facts come from the reference itself (cross-platform ShareX.ImageEditor, read directly and confirmed online): margin 80, padding 40, smart padding on by default, corner radius 20, shadow radius 30 with no separate toggle (0 removes it), transparent default, solid #FF222222, gradient #FFDD2476 -> #FFFF512F, smart padding = the source's top-left pixel target with tolerance 30 per RGBA channel (inclusive, per-edge uniform-border insets, self-disabled without a border, annotations excluded from detection), and the canvas shadow's blur/offset/alpha facts (Blur = radius, OffsetY = 10, black at alpha 80/255). Built as CanvasAction::Background in src/image-editor/CanvasOperations: the composed geometry is inner-to-outer (optionally smart-clipped) content, padding band in the source's exact top-left colour, rounded card (deterministic 4x4 supersampled coverage), gaussian shadow reusing the house kernel (sigma = radius / 3, the blurredClamp convention, unclamped so the shadow fades at the canvas bound), and a square margin band in the chosen kind; annotations translate with the content and clip against the composed canvas; validation is typed with no partial outputs. The shadow reuses effects/EffectSupport's gaussianBlur255 - xerahs_core now links xerahs_effects PRIVATE (no cycle: effects depend only on Qt) instead of duplicating a second blur kernel. The editor journey is the Image > Background dialog (app/CanvasBackgroundDialog, pure form; the committed operation and its typed failures run through the shared canvas worker with the busy overlay) committing one history entry; the saved PNG carries the composed pixels. Tests: seven core tests pin the decided geometry, kinds, smart clip (the compose equals the clipped content exactly), hand-derived gaussian shadow values (70 and 7 at the pinned pixels, derived from the decided kernel and geometry), rounding, validation/cancellation and annotation translation, plus the EditorWindowTest journey (apply, dirty, one undoable entry, save, the composed pixels reload; undo restores the exact prior document) and a localization test. The smart-padding scan, the shadow's +10 drop and the corner rounding were each proven red by disabling the rule and watching the matching tests fail. Full suite 186/186. Remaining: the image kind behind the inserted-image safety rules, the Wallpaper kind (a reference extra outside the SPEC's four), gradient presets, and EC-014's flatten background clause reconciliation (the committed model bakes an applied background into the source, so the follow-up is the clause's dedicated evidence).

Decided and built 2026-11-23 (backlog item 2's other half, first slice - decision ES-020-RETENTION-2026-11-23, resolved by the build loop under delegated owner-block authority; no contract text change so no version bump, the EU-004-recognition-gate precedent): ES-020's named policy gate ('configured editor temp/recovery retention and secure-delete limits') is settled with three validated settings - editorRetention.temporaryDays (default 1, the landed 24 h bound made configurable, 0..30, 0 = sweep every startup, the reference CleanupManager's own wholesale startup-clean, safe on POSIX because an in-flight task's open handle survives unlinking), editorRetention.recoveryDays (default 7, 0..90, 0 = count-only, today's behaviour) and editorRetention.secureDelete (default off, matching the reference which never overwrites) - with General-tab rows carrying shred's documented in-place-overwrite caveat in plain English. Retention is enforced at startup once the settings store has loaded (the sweeps moved after the store's construction in main.cpp so the configured values govern them): the temp sweep keeps the private-directory fd checks (0700 dir, regular 0600 user-owned nlink-1 files) and adds the configured bound, and the new recovery age sweep reuses the store's per-file lock, exited-owner and valid-savedAt pattern so a live editor's record is never an age candidate and corrupt records stay with the listing's set-aside path. Secure delete, when on, overwrites with one zero-fill pass and fdatasync before unlink through a shared storage primitive (storage/PrivateJsonFile's overwriteForRemoval - no duplicated kernel between the two sweeps). Tests: the settings defaults/round-trip/repair/matrix rows (ApplicationSettingsTest), the General-tab dialog rows (prefill, Apply persists, Cancel keeps, the caveat visible), the configured temp sweep (0 = every startup, 3 keeps, 1 removes) and the recovery sweep (retention 0 is count-only; the bound prunes exactly the old exited-owner record; the live owner and the corrupt record stay; secure delete zeroes). The overwrite is observed the honest POSIX way - the swept file's still-open descriptor reads zeros after the sweep. The recovery live-owner guard, the recovery age bound and the overwrite call were each proven red by disabling the rule and watching the matching tests fail. En route: the every-QLineEdit-has-a-name invariant caught my first retention spins (the house spin() helper names the spin's internal lineEdit - reuse it, do not hand-roll); the value-matrix ledger caught the three new keys needing good/bad rows; and the capture-tab group enumeration was scoped to its tab now that the General tab carries a group box too.
